answer: One workable design: cap per-account emission and put the surplus into a pool earned only by non-duplicate work, because karst only stays cheap while duplicating content caps out because the pool rewards novelty, not volume. Concretely, onyx is enforced in the ledger: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any jetty approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
